style: Refined interface layers with transparent backgrounds

prompts.browser:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: a single transparent desktop browser layer used inside an animated 3D portfolio illustration.
Edit target: the attached browser.webp. Replace its crude four-block wireframe with a beautifully finished, finely detailed UX experimentation interface. Keep the same broad landscape browser silhouette, frontal orthographic view, transparent background, isolated object and wide 760:420 composition. The CSS will rotate it, so do not introduce perspective.
Design direction: precise and understated, elegant high-fidelity software UI. Much thinner strokes and framing, regular/medium small sans-serif typography, refined spacing, restrained cool white and warm ivory surfaces, a slim silver rim with subtle bevel and highlights, very soft physically plausible shadow and shallow depth. Preserve blue #0849b6 accents, charcoal #111920, off-white #fbf7ec, tiny coral #ef3625 details. Avoid thick outlines, huge rounded blobs, bold labels, toy-like clay rendering, bloom or neon.
Show a real detailed browser toolbar with tiny window dots, one slim tab, address field; then a product named "Signal" with a compact left navigation rail. Main heading "Experiment overview". Small A / B segmented selector, a delicate line chart with axes and faint grid, two small metric summaries, a slim table of variants and a status column. Fine 1px dividers, small icons, subtle tonal changes, careful alignment and a few tiny blue progress bars add craft. Illustration data is fictional; no huge percentage-lift claims. Most of the refinement should be visual, not big text.
Only produce the single browser panel, no phone, no heatmap overlay, no other floating panels, no external labels, no backdrop or ground plane. The panel must fit inside the image with a narrow transparent gutter. Genuine alpha transparency, not a checkerboard painted into the image.
prompts.mobile:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: a single isolated layer of an animated 3D illustration for a UX engineer portfolio. Edit Image 1 (the target); Image 2 is only the style and UI reference, never include that browser in the output. Use a refined, detailed, understated high-fidelity software UI: fine 1px dividers, restrained typography mostly regular weight, tiny crisp outline icons, careful alignment and micro-details, softly beveled rim, faint material highlights, shallow believable depth and soft shadow. Avoid thick black frames, giant typography, placeholder skeleton bars, flat chunky shapes, toy clay rendering, blown-out highlights or heavy glow. Palette from the reference: blue #0849b6, warm off-white #fbf7ec, charcoal #111920 and sparse coral #ef3625 details. Keep the target object's own aspect ratio, face-on orthographic view (CSS adds rotation later), narrow transparent gutter and fully transparent background. No other objects, composition, scenery, external labels, ground plane, black backdrop or checkerboard. Keep all edges clean and antialiased.
Primary request: Redesign the phone layer as a beautifully machined slim graphite smartphone, portrait 240:430 proportions. Extremely fine bezel and subtle polished edge, a small speaker/camera detail and understated side controls. Its light screen shows the responsive version of the Signal experiment interface in Image 2: compact status bar, Signal wordmark, a small A/B segmented selector, a delicate multi-point blue versus gray chart with axis ticks and faint grid, two small metric chips, two slim variant rows with status dots, fine bottom navigation icons and a thin home indicator. Use predominantly regular-weight type. Any data should read as placeholders or "Sample". No huge percentage claim. The handset itself is the only object and should fill about 91 percent of the portrait canvas.

prompts.ticket:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit Image 1 (the target); Image 2 supplies only material, edge treatment and typography style. Output one small isolated interface status card, face-on orthographic, with a narrow transparent gutter. It will be an independently animated 3D layer in a portfolio. The user dislikes chunky/bold/raw assets, so use light regular typography, fine 1px lines, exquisitely aligned micro-details, restrained colors, subtle surface shading, a very slim beveled rim and soft shadow. No oversized lettering, giant icons, fat pill shapes, neon glow, thick outlines or cartoon rendering. No other windows, objects, external labels, background, floor or checkerboard. True alpha transparency outside the card silhouette.
Primary request: Redesign the ticket card, wide 350:112 proportions. Dark graphite surface with a subtle cool highlight, tiny outlined task icon at left. A fine upper row reads "CRO-184" and a discreet "Ready for UAT" status with a tiny muted blue dot. A smaller secondary line reads "Experience / Variant B". Add a hairline divider, three delicate checklist ticks along the bottom with compact labels "UI", "Tracking", "QA", and a subtle overlapping pair of tiny initials circles at the far right. Do not use a giant checkbox, big filled badges, or bold headlines. Only the slim ticket card.
